title: UPRIGHT TIMBER SPINNING WHEEL ...
reason: Complete working-style timber spinning wheel with carders, bobbins and winder; maker not shown but hobby demand makes it plausibly worth real money.
findings: Complete-looking upright (Saxony style) timber spinning wheel with a long treadle board, flyer assembly and several bobbins fitted, some with yarn. The layout resembles the Ashford Traditional pattern from New Zealand, but no maker's transfer, plate or burn mark is visible in either photo, so the maker is unproven. Accessories on the floor: a pair of wooden hand carders (blue card cloth visible), a boxed 'WOOL WINDER' (white box, red lettering, no maker's name legible), spare bobbins, a wooden-backed wool comb with steel tines, a plastic reel with a red 'Luc...' label (probably an unrelated wire reel) and a small amber bottle with a green and white label (probably wheel oil, text not legible). Not a spirits lot.
condition: Wheel looks solid and complete with drive band and bobbins; normal wear and darkening. Cannot tell if it runs freely or if the flyer hooks and orifice are intact. Accessories are used and the box shows age marks.
rescore_note: Complete Saxony style wheel that resembles an Ashford Traditional (the boxed wool winder hints at it, but no maker mark seen) with carders, comb and spare bobbins; working order unchecked; steady hobby demand puts it at the upper end of the $80-200 band. Estimate only, no live comps.
